selectionBasis: Cached audit queue only; full audit is stale because @paddletoday/geo is unavailable. Every selected site was checked against current or explicitly dated primary/operator evidence.

decisions.coordinateRole: mapped water-entry feature; approximately 50 ft uncertainty
decisions.method: NPS confirms Steel Creek as a public Buffalo River access. The old NPS coordinate describes the campground, not the river entry. OSM slipway node 12544125462 is the specific nearby water-entry feature; rounded to six decimals in route data.

evidence.finding: NPS names Steel Creek in its public river access ladder and mileage.
Feature is tagged leisure=slipway and access=yes; coordinate source, not the legal-access authority.
NPS campground GPS is a separate facility anchor and must not be used as the water-entry point.

decisions.publication: Seven dependent routes withheld pending canonical geometry and served-catalog regeneration.
decisions.reopenWhen: Regenerate and inspect each route geometry against the corrected entry, then rebuild the served catalog and verify route endpoints.

decisions.method: Keep the coordinate as a broad access-area anchor. WGFD confirms the public area, primitive ramp, pedestrian river access, parking and restrooms; its embedded map center does not isolate the exact ramp-water entry. Increase the unjustifiably precise 25 ft uncertainty to 300 ft.

evidence.finding: Current manager page identifies the public access and describes separate primitive boat-ramp and pedestrian access.

decisions.publication: Route remains public as a documented access-area anchor; no coordinate snap applied.
decisions.reopenWhen: Only replace the anchor if a current WGFD ramp feature or imagery identifies an exact water-entry point.

decisions.coordinateRole: mapped boat-ramp/slipway feature; approximately 50 ft uncertainty
decisions.method: American Whitewater identifies the City Park boat ramp as the standard Little Salmon take-out near Highway 95 mile 195.7. Riggins City Council records support current city ramp work. OSM node 7560987269 is the named City Park slipway and supplies the feature coordinate; source precision is rounded to six decimals.

evidence.finding: Identifies Riggins City Park as the best/standard public boat-ramp take-out for the Little Salmon run.
Named Riggins City Park Boat Ramp, leisure=slipway; coordinate source.
June 2025 council record references boat-ramp project closeout; direct file retrieval returned 403, so browser-extracted source text is recorded without a local file hash.
June 2024 council minutes reference the ramp project; direct file retrieval returned 403, so browser-extracted source text is recorded without a local file hash.

decisions.publication: Route withheld pending geometry and catalog regeneration.
decisions.reopenWhen: Regenerate the reach to the ramp feature, inspect endpoint and river-mile fit, rebuild catalog assets, and then clear the hold.

decisions.coordinateRole: official DNR public-access feature/access-area anchor; 50 ft uncertainty
decisions.method: Iowa DNR feature OBJECTID 896 / GlobalID 5a010dab-cd81-48be-af79-ad07c89abff7 matches Wilkinson Pioneer Park, Cerro Gordo County, and Shell Rock River. DNR reports 75 ft parking-to-access. County materials independently identify canoe floating there. Use GIS point as an access-area anchor, not a surveyed shoreline entry.

evidence.finding: Current Iowa DNR feature with matching name, county, owner, waterbody, geometry, and 75 ft parking-to-access.
County confirms canoe-floating and public park use.

decisions.publication: Route withheld pending canonical geometry and served-catalog regeneration.
decisions.reopenWhen: Regenerate source geometry, inspect endpoint fit on the Shell Rock reach, rebuild the catalog, and verify all endpoint copies.

decisions.site: Driscoll Road Landing public canoe/kayak access
decisions.coordinateRole: documented public access-area anchor; 450 ft uncertainty
decisions.method: The 2026 Saratoga Springs Open Space Plan supports public canoe/kayak access at Driscoll Road, but reviewed sources do not isolate the exact water entry. Keep the existing access-area anchor and its stated uncertainty; do not move it toward hydrography.

evidence.finding: Current city plan supports public canoe/kayak access at the landing; no exact entry coordinate was established.

decisions.publication: Existing access-area anchor retained; no hold added.
decisions.reopenWhen: Revisit if the city publishes a feature-specific launch coordinate or current map/imagery resolves the entry.

decisions.method: Franklin County identifies Waid Park as a public recreation facility with kayak/canoe and river access; the Blueway maps support the access corridor. Existing point is a park/facility anchor, not an exact surveyed water-entry point.

evidence.finding: County facility page confirms park, river access and kayak/canoe launch context.
County Blueway materials support the named access in the route chain.

decisions.publication: Existing documented facility anchor retained; no hold added.
decisions.reopenWhen: Revisit only if a current mapped launch feature is needed to distinguish the exact shoreline entry from park staging.

decisions.site: Lewis River Channel northern shallow section
decisions.method: NPS describes the northern channel mile as shallow and rocky where upstream travel can require wading and lining. The route source itself labeled this point not a formal landing. Remove it from accessPoints and retain the safety warning.

evidence.finding: Current NPS boating guidance identifies the Lewis River Channel and its operating limits.
NPS boating booklet describes the northern mile as a wade/line condition, not an access facility.

decisions.publication: False access marker removed; route held until served catalog is regenerated. Safety guidance remains.
decisions.reopenWhen: Do not restore as an access point. Add a marker only if a public landing is separately identified.

decisions.coordinateRole: official DNR concrete public-access feature/access-area anchor; 50 ft uncertainty
decisions.method: Iowa DNR OBJECTID 805 / GlobalID b2b6566e-9cd3-43a3-8a75-f45f201c03c2 is the Middle Raccoon River Access in Guthrie County, with concrete surface and 10 ft parking-to-access. Guthrie County lists 248th Trail as the intermediate Route A access 3.2 river miles below P-28. This disambiguates it from the separate Cowles terminal.

evidence.finding: Current DNR feature has matching site, county and waterbody; concrete surface, 10 ft parking-to-access, exact geometry.
County lists 248th Trail in the public Middle Raccoon Route A chain, about 3.2 miles below P-28.

decisions.publication: Route withheld pending canonical geometry and served-catalog regeneration.
decisions.reopenWhen: Regenerate the route, verify its 3.2-mile intermediate access and both terminals, rebuild the served catalog, then clear the hold.

decisions.site: Givhans Ferry State Park river access
decisions.coordinateRole: park/drop-off area anchor; exact open public water entry unresolved
decisions.method: Current South Carolina State Parks page describes a drop-off area and a boat ramp three miles from the park, and warns that cabin-area river stairs remain closed. Keep the old point only as a labeled park-area anchor, do not call it a ramp, hold the three terminal routes, and remove Givhans as a promised intermediate bailout from independent Mars Oldfield routes.

evidence.finding: Current manager page carries the river-stairs closure notice and distinguishes the park drop-off from a boat ramp three miles away.
Historical guide gives general landing context but cannot establish present access or override current closure.

decisions.publication: Three routes with Givhans as a terminal are held. Two other routes remain independently valid after Givhans bailout language was removed.
decisions.reopenWhen: State Parks or another manager confirms the currently open legal launch/carry and the precise route endpoint; then update the coordinate and route text.

decisions.method: American Whitewater/RiverFacts identifies an endpoint coordinate but does not establish lawful public landing, parking or a safe carry at the high-school frontage. No manager-backed replacement was found. Keep the existing record for review and withhold the Class IV–V route; do not substitute a nearby bridge.

evidence.finding: Route description and endpoint pin are present; legal access/parking is not established by that point.

decisions.publication: Route held; coordinate retained as an unverified source record, not public access.
decisions.reopenWhen: A land manager confirms legal public access, parking and carry, and a precise water-entry coordinate is independently identified.
